anlamlar.en: to go towards a place
ornekler: We made for the exit.
The ship made for the harbor.

anlamlar.en: to help to make something possible
ornekler: Good planning makes for a successful trip.
Short sentences make for easy reading.

anlamlar.en: to leave quickly, especially to escape
ornekler: The thieves made off in a stolen car.
He made off with all the money.

anlamlar.tr: seçebilmek, zorla görmek ya da duymak
anlamlar.en: to be able to see, hear or understand something with difficulty
ornekler: I could just make out a figure in the dark.
I can't make out what he's saying.

anlamlar.en: to understand someone or something
ornekler: I can't make her out at all.
Can you make out this handwriting?

anlamlar.en: to claim that something is true when it may not be
ornekler: He made out that he was rich.
She's not as bad as people make out.

anlamlar.en: to invent a story, excuse or explanation
ornekler: He made up an excuse for being late.
I think she made the whole story up.

anlamlar.en: to form a particular amount or part of something
ornekler: Women make up 60% of our students.
The team is made up of five people.

anlamlar.en: to become friends again after an argument
ornekler: They argued, but they made up the next day.
Have you two made up yet?

anlamlar.en: to put make-up on someone's face
ornekler: She made herself up for the party.
The actors were made up before the show.

anlamlar.en: to do something good to replace something lost or done badly
ornekler: I bought her flowers to make up for being late.
Nothing can make up for the loss of a child.

anlamlar.tr: vakit öldürmek, ciddiye almamak, aptalca davranmak
anlamlar.en: to behave in a silly way or waste time
ornekler: Stop messing around and do your homework.
We spent the day messing around on the beach.

anlamlar.en: to lose an opportunity to do or have something good
ornekler: Don't miss out on this great offer.
I missed out on the party because I was ill.

anlamlar.en: to not include someone or something
ornekler: You've missed out an important point.
Don't miss anyone out.

anlamlar.en: to think that one person or thing is another
ornekler: People often mix up the twins.
I always mix up these two words.

anlamlar.en: to put things in the wrong order
ornekler: Someone has mixed up all my papers.
Don't mix up the files.

anlamlar.en: to start living in a new home
ornekler: We're moving in next week.
She moved in with her boyfriend.

anlamlar.tr: (başka bir konuya, yere) geçmek, devam etmek
anlamlar.en: to leave a place or start doing something new
ornekler: Let's move on to the next topic.
After five years in the job, she decided to move on.

anlamlar.en: to accept that a situation has changed and start thinking about other things
ornekler: It's time to move on and forget about him.
You need to move on with your life.

anlamlar.en: to stop living in a particular home
ornekler: He moved out of his parents' house at 18.
Our neighbors are moving out.

anlamlar.en: to make a list of possibilities smaller
ornekler: We've narrowed the list down to three candidates.
Can you narrow down your search?

anlamlar.en: to write something down so that you will not forget it
ornekler: I noted down her address.
Note down any words you don't know.

anlamlar.en: to start to talk about your feelings
ornekler: It took him a long time to open up to me.
She finally opened up about her problems.

anlamlar.en: to make something possible or available
ornekler: The new road will open up the region to tourists.
Learning English opens up many opportunities.

anlamlar.en: to choose not to be part of an activity or agreement
ornekler: You can opt out of the scheme at any time.
Several countries opted out of the agreement.

anlamlar.en: to admit that you have done something wrong
ornekler: Nobody owned up to breaking the window.
He owned up to his mistake.

anlamlar.en: to die (used to be polite)
ornekler: Her grandfather passed away last year.
He passed away peacefully in his sleep.

anlamlar.en: to go past a person or place
ornekler: I pass by the bakery every morning.
A car passed by slowly.

anlamlar.en: to give information or an object to someone else
ornekler: Can you pass on a message to her?
Please read this and pass it on.

anlamlar.en: to give a disease to someone
ornekler: The virus can be passed on through touch.
Wash your hands so you don't pass on your cold.

anlamlar.en: to become unconscious for a short time
ornekler: He passed out because of the heat.
She almost passed out when she saw the blood.

anlamlar.en: to not use an opportunity
ornekler: I can't pass up a chance like this.
He passed up the offer of a free trip.

anlamlar.en: to give back money that you borrowed
ornekler: I'll pay you back next week.
He still hasn't paid back the loan.

anlamlar.en: to do something unpleasant to someone because they did something bad to you
ornekler: I'll pay him back for what he did.
She wanted to pay them back for the insult.

anlamlar.en: to gradually stop using or providing something
ornekler: The old system will be phased out next year.
Plastic bags are being phased out.

anlamlar.en: to treat someone badly or unfairly, especially repeatedly
ornekler: Stop picking on your little brother!
The other kids picked on him at school.

anlamlar.en: to increase in amount, especially in a way that is difficult to deal with
ornekler: Work keeps piling up on my desk.
The bills were piling up.

anlamlar.en: to make something seem less important or less bad than it really is
ornekler: The government tried to play down the problem.
He played down his role in the success.

anlamlar.en: to connect a piece of electrical equipment to a supply of electricity
ornekler: Is the TV plugged in?
Plug in your phone to charge it.

anlamlar.en: to tell someone something that they did not know or had not noticed
ornekler: She pointed out a mistake in my essay.
I should point out that this is only a theory.

anlamlar.en: to show someone where something is by pointing
ornekler: He pointed out the house where he was born.
The guide pointed out the old castle.

anlamlar.en: to visit someone for a short time
ornekler: I'll pop in to see you later.
She popped in on her way to work.

anlamlar.en: to appear suddenly or unexpectedly
ornekler: A message popped up on the screen.
New cafes keep popping up in the area.

anlamlar.en: to destroy a building or other structure
ornekler: The old cinema was pulled down.
They're going to pull down these houses.

anlamlar.en: to move to the side of the road and stop (a vehicle)
ornekler: The driver pulled in at a gas station.
The bus pulled in at the stop.

anlamlar.en: to succeed in doing something difficult
ornekler: They pulled off a surprising win.
I don't know how she pulled it off.

anlamlar.en: to stop being involved in an activity or agreement
ornekler: He pulled out of the race with an injury.
The company pulled out of the deal.

anlamlar.en: to drive onto a road or move to another part of the road
ornekler: The car pulled out in front of me.
The train pulled out of the station.

anlamlar.en: to move a vehicle to the side of the road and stop
ornekler: The police officer told him to pull over.
I pulled over to check the map.

anlamlar.en: to recover from a serious illness or difficult situation
ornekler: The doctors think she'll pull through.
We'll pull through somehow.

anlamlar.en: to stop a vehicle
ornekler: A taxi pulled up outside the hotel.
He pulled up at the traffic lights.

anlamlar.en: to move a chair closer to something
ornekler: Pull up a chair and join us.
She pulled up a seat next to me.

anlamlar.en: to explain your ideas clearly so that people understand them
ornekler: She put her point across very well.
He found it hard to put across his message.

anlamlar.en: to save money or time for a particular purpose
ornekler: I put aside some money every month.
Put aside an hour a day for reading.

anlamlar.tr: bir kenara bırakmak, göz ardı etmek
anlamlar.en: to not think about a problem or feeling so that you can deal with something else
ornekler: Let's put aside our differences.
Try to put your worries aside.

anlamlar.en: to put something in the place where you usually keep it
ornekler: Put your toys away, please.
She put the dishes away.

anlamlar.en: to return something to the place where it was
ornekler: Put the book back on the shelf when you've finished.
Don't forget to put the milk back in the fridge.

anlamlar.en: to change the date or time of an event to a later one
ornekler: The meeting has been put back to Friday.
The launch was put back a week.

anlamlar.en: to put something on the floor or another surface
ornekler: Put down that knife!
She put the phone down.

anlamlar.en: to write something
ornekler: Put your name down on the list.
I've put down everything I remember.

anlamlar.en: to criticize someone and make them feel stupid
ornekler: He's always putting his wife down.
Don't let anyone put you down.

anlamlar.en: to stop a rebellion by force
ornekler: The army put down the revolt.
The protests were quickly put down.

anlamlar.en: to state an idea or opinion so that people can consider it
ornekler: She put forward a plan to save money.
Several theories have been put forward.

anlamlar.en: to spend time or energy doing something
ornekler: She put in a lot of work on the project.
He puts in long hours at the office.

anlamlar.en: to fit equipment in a building
ornekler: We're having a new kitchen put in.
They put in central heating.

anlamlar.en: to decide to do something later
ornekler: Don't put off going to the dentist.
The match was put off because of rain.

anlamlar.en: to make someone dislike something or not want to do something
ornekler: The smell put me off my food.
Don't let one bad experience put you off.

anlamlar.en: to put clothes, shoes or jewelry on your body
ornekler: Put on your coat, it's cold.
She put on her glasses to read.

anlamlar.en: to make a piece of equipment start working
ornekler: Can you put the light on?
Put some music on.

anlamlar.en: to become heavier
ornekler: I've put on two kilos this month.
He's put on a lot of weight.

anlamlar.en: to organize an event or performance
ornekler: The school is putting on a play.
They put on a concert for charity.

anlamlar.en: to pretend to have a particular feeling or way of speaking
ornekler: She put on a brave face.
He's not really angry – he's just putting it on.

anlamlar.en: to make a fire or cigarette stop burning
ornekler: Firefighters put out the fire quickly.
Please put out your cigarette.

anlamlar.en: to cause someone extra work or trouble
ornekler: I don't want to put you out.
Are you sure it won't put you out?

anlamlar.en: to produce information and make it available
ornekler: The police put out a description of the man.
The company put out a statement.

anlamlar.en: to connect someone to the person they want to speak to on the phone
ornekler: Could you put me through to the manager?
Hold on, I'll put you through.

anlamlar.en: to make someone experience something unpleasant
ornekler: She put her parents through a lot of worry.
I'm sorry to put you through this.

anlamlar.en: to make something by joining its parts
ornekler: It took us an hour to put the shelf together.
Can you help me put this puzzle together?

anlamlar.en: to prepare something by collecting ideas or information
ornekler: She put together a report on the project.
We need to put together a team.

anlamlar.en: to put something on a wall or build something
ornekler: We put up some pictures in the living room.
They put up a tent by the lake.

anlamlar.en: to increase the price or amount of something
ornekler: The shop has put up its prices.
They put the rent up again.

anlamlar.en: to let someone stay in your home for a short time
ornekler: Can you put me up for the night?
My friends put us up while we were in London.

anlamlar.en: to accept unpleasant behavior or a situation without complaining
ornekler: I can't put up with this noise any longer.
How do you put up with him?

anlamlar.en: to read something and say the words so that other people can hear
ornekler: The teacher read out the names.
Can you read out the results?

anlamlar.en: to telephone someone again, or to telephone someone who rang you
ornekler: I'm busy now – can I ring you back?
She said she'd ring back later.

anlamlar.en: to telephone someone
ornekler: I rang up the cinema to book tickets.
Why don't you ring her up?

anlamlar.en: to charge someone too much money for something
ornekler: Tourists often get ripped off in this area.
That shop really ripped me off.

anlamlar.en: to decide that something is not possible or suitable
ornekler: The police have ruled out murder.
We can't rule out the possibility of rain.

anlamlar.en: to meet someone or find something by chance
ornekler: I ran across an old friend in town.
I ran across this book in a second-hand shop.

anlamlar.en: to chase someone or something
ornekler: The dog ran after the ball.
He ran after the bus but missed it.

anlamlar.en: to leave a place or person secretly and suddenly
ornekler: The boy ran away from home.
Don't run away from your problems.

anlamlar.en: to lose power or become weaker
ornekler: My phone battery has run down.
The town has been run down for years.

anlamlar.en: to hit someone with a vehicle and injure or kill them
ornekler: He was run down by a bus.
A cyclist was run down on this road.

anlamlar.en: to criticize someone or something, often unfairly
ornekler: Stop running yourself down!
He's always running down his colleagues.

anlamlar.en: to meet someone you know by chance
ornekler: I ran into Sarah at the supermarket.
Guess who I ran into today?

anlamlar.en: to start to experience a difficult situation
ornekler: The project ran into problems.
They ran into debt.

anlamlar.en: to hit something with a vehicle
ornekler: The car ran into a tree.
A bus ran into the back of our car.

anlamlar.en: to be completely used so that there is nothing left
ornekler: The milk has run out.
Time is running out.

anlamlar.en: to use all of something and have nothing left
ornekler: We've run out of coffee.
The car ran out of gas.

anlamlar.en: to hit someone or something with a vehicle and drive over them
ornekler: He was nearly run over by a truck.
Our cat was run over last week.

anlamlar.en: to continue past the expected finishing time
ornekler: The meeting ran over by twenty minutes.
Sorry, the class ran over.

anlamlar.en: to repeat something or explain something quickly
ornekler: Let's run through the plan once more.
The actors ran through their lines.

anlamlar.en: to do something too quickly without thinking carefully
ornekler: Don't rush into marriage.
We shouldn't rush into a decision.
